themes.description: Products and infrastructure facilitating financial transactions between consumers, merchants, and financial institutions, including gateways, processors, and digital transfer methods.

linked_companies.description: Operates a global digital payment network that facilitates electronic funds transfers among consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and government entities through extensive credit, debit, and prepaid card infrastructure.
linked_companies.evidence: Visa operates as the leading hyperscaler of payments globally, with its core consumer, commercial, and money movement platforms driving the entirety of its $11.2 billion net revenue and $3.7 trillion in payments volume during the second quarter of fiscal 2026. To facilitate this fundamental financial infrastructure, the company leverages its proprietary Visa as a Service stack and gateway solutions like Visa Direct to empower an ecosystem of fintechs and digital wallets, including direct integrations with TikTok, X Money, and Japan's PayPay. Furthermore, Visa expands its transaction processing architecture through targeted local workforce deployments, maintaining over 6,000 dedicated operational employees in Europe alone, alongside major cash acquisitions of issuer processing platforms like Pismo, Prisma, and Newpay.
linked_companies.name: VISA INC-CLASS A SHARES

linked_companies.description: Operates a global technology network that provides comprehensive payment solutions, facilitating secure electronic transactions, card processing, and financial transfers across consumer and commercial markets.
linked_companies.evidence: Mastercard's corporate framework is structured explicitly around its global payment network, dividing operations into Consumer Payments, Commercial Flows, and Value-Added Services. The company actively upgrades this infrastructure by deploying near-real-time settlement protocols, advancing network tokenization, and scaling Click to Pay capabilities across hundreds of millions of worldwide acceptance locations. These transaction processing solutions serve as Mastercard's foundational revenue engine, prompting continuous capital allocation into multi-rail technology and strategic capacity reinvestments to support hundreds of billions of switched transactions annually.
linked_companies.name: MASTERCARD INC - A

linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive digital platform that enables consumers and merchants to conduct secure online, mobile, and in-person transactions through digital wallets and payment processing services.
linked_companies.evidence: PayPal's fundamental identity as a digital finance provider is reinforced by its recent organizational realignment into three dedicated payment-focused divisions: Checkout Solutions, Consumer Financial Services, and Payment Services & Crypto. Transaction processing serves as the absolute core of the company's financial model, most recently generating $7.5 billion—roughly 90% of its total quarterly revenue—from over $464 billion in total payment volume. To defend this vast two-sided network infrastructure, PayPal is directing its primary capital investments toward a module-by-module technology modernization of its fintech platforms. This strategy includes accelerating global checkout enhancements and scaling mobile-first omnichannel offerings like Venmo, Tap to Pay, and newly launched contactless NFC wallets.
linked_companies.name: PAYPAL HOLDINGS INC

linked_companies.description: Delivers comprehensive corporate payment solutions that encompass fleet mobility, corporate travel, and B2B accounts payable automation to streamline global business transactions and expense management.
linked_companies.evidence: Corpay's core strategic priority is rotating its portfolio to provide global corporate payment solutions, focusing specifically on B2B transactions, accounts payable automation, and cross-border platforms. Management recently redirected internal sales and marketing capital explicitly into its Corporate Payments and Vehicle Payments divisions, which together command 85% of the company's total revenue and processed $82 billion in organic corporate spend during a single quarter. To expand these financial technology capabilities, Corpay has executed over $3 billion in foundational payment acquisitions, including Alpha and AvidXchange, alongside securing an exclusive joint-sale cross-border partnership and equity investment from Mastercard. Ultimately, Corpay operates entirely as a dedicated fintech provider relying on proprietary software and digital networks to help businesses manage, digitize, and control their workflow expenses.
linked_companies.name: CORPAY INC

linked_companies.description: Provides electronic payment and banking solutions that facilitate real-time transaction processing and digital payment infrastructure for financial institutions and merchants.
linked_companies.evidence: ACI Worldwide operates as a pure-play payments infrastructure provider, deriving its entire $426 million quarterly revenue in Q2 2026 directly from its dedicated Payment Software and Biller segments. The company's business model relies exclusively on facilitating global financial transactions through flagship platforms like the cloud-native ACI Connetic for intelligent payment orchestration and Speedpay ONE for mobile-first digital bill payments. Underlining its foundational role in the global financial ecosystem, ACI maintains certifications across hundreds of international networks and provides the central processing infrastructure that supports over two-thirds of Fedwire traffic, approximately 15% of Swift payments, and 11 central banks worldwide.
linked_companies.name: ACI WORLDWIDE INC

themes.description: Innovative tools and applications developed to support and improve processes in the retail sector, including point-of-sale systems, inventory management, and customer analytics.

linked_companies.description: Delivers comprehensive point-of-sale systems, self-checkout technologies, and cloud-based digital commerce platforms that optimize store operations and enhance the customer experience across the retail sector.
linked_companies.evidence: NCR Voyix functions primarily as a retail technology provider, centering its operations around the ongoing deployment of its cloud-native Voyix Commerce Platform, Voyix POS, and Picklist Assist self-checkout systems. The company's dedicated Retail segment dictates its financial identity, generating $427 million in Q2 2026 to account for over 70% of total revenue. Strategic execution involves migrating enterprise customers from legacy architectures to modern microservices, highlighted by a recent Q2 deployment of computer vision technology across 35,000 self-checkout lanes and an expansion to 83,000 active platform sites. This unified commerce focus is structurally reinforced by a dedicated executive leadership team, including a President of Retail and a Chief Product Officer, managing integrated hardware and software implementations across thousands of global storefronts.
linked_companies.name: NCR VOYIX CORP

linked_companies.description: Delivers an integrated, cloud-based point-of-sale and management platform that combines payment processing, digital ordering, and operational software to streamline workflows across the restaurant and retail food service industry.
linked_companies.evidence: Toast is evolving its vertically integrated point-of-sale platform from its core restaurant ecosystem into a full system of record for enterprise retail and independent grocers. The company's engineering teams are directly adapting their existing software and hardware architecture to manage complex retail environments, emphasizing heavy inventory volumes, massive SKU variants, and supplier connectivity. To accelerate this expansion across its 171,000 live locations, Toast has deployed dedicated internal R&D allocations and scaled a specialized go-to-market team focused exclusively on tailoring point-of-sale capabilities for convenience stores, bottle shops, and grocery chains.
linked_companies.name: TOAST INC-CLASS A

linked_companies.description: Provides a comprehensive suite of enterprise e-commerce platforms, fulfillment software, and in-store digital integrations that enable grocery retailers to optimize omnichannel operations and enhance customer shopping experiences.
linked_companies.evidence: Instacart's alignment with Retail Technology Solutions is driven by its end-to-end grocery enterprise platform, which operates as a primary growth engine and generates the company's entire $1.02 billion top line. The company supplies purpose-built retail infrastructure, utilizing its Storefront Pro software to power over 380 grocery e-commerce sites and deploying in-store modernization tools like FoodStorm, Carrot Tags, and computer-vision shelf tracking. To expand this technological ecosystem globally, Instacart is heavily investing in specialized R&D and strategic talent acquisitions, most recently integrating the Instaleap team and deploying AI-powered Caper smart carts across hundreds of cities. Through these dedicated hardware and software suites, the company acts as the foundational technology provider bridging e-commerce and physical store operations for its retail partners.
linked_companies.name: MAPLEBEAR INC

linked_companies.description: Delivers advanced supply chain and omnichannel commerce software that provides retailers with integrated warehouse management, inventory optimization, and point-of-sale capabilities to unify back-end logistics and front-end customer experiences.
linked_companies.evidence: Manhattan Associates anchors its enterprise software ecosystem in retail technology solutions, recently securing its largest-ever Order Management System (OMS) bookings deal with a global retailer while continuing to convert tier-one brands across the wellness and auto parts sectors. The company integrates robust inventory management, fulfillment, and transportation APIs, optimizing facility peak flow logic through tools like a customized Foundry agent that recently drove a five percent improvement in order cycle times for a major U.S. distribution center. To further modernize retail store operations, Manhattan directs its R&D funding toward its cloud-native, mobile-first Active Store and Active Point-of-Sale applications. These specialized front-end tools natively embed Agentic AI to deliver prescriptive recommendations that enhance physical store associate efficiency, cementing retail point-of-commerce execution as the core driver of the company's omnichannel software platform.
linked_companies.name: MANHATTAN ASSOCIATES INC

linked_companies.description: Provides specialized hardware and software, including mobile computers, barcode scanners, and RFID systems, designed to optimize inventory tracking, streamline checkout processes, and improve overall operational efficiency in retail environments.
linked_companies.evidence: Zebra integrates point-of-sale systems, self-service kiosks, and interactive touchscreen displays into its Connected Frontline segment, a capability directly expanded by the $1.3 billion acquisition of Elo Touch. As a stated global leader in the Automatic Identification and Data Capture industry, the company provides fixed and handheld RFID readers designed to modernize physical store operations and retail checkout processes. Zebra embeds these hardware assets within its AI-powered modern store architecture, outfitting retailers with mobile computing tools to execute omnichannel strategies, track real-time inventory, and reduce shrink.
linked_companies.name: ZEBRA TECHNOLOGIES CORP-CL A

themes.description: Conducting retail, services, and transactions via electronic platforms, harnessing digital and internet technologies to facilitate shopping, banking, and information dissemination.

linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive e-commerce platform supported by an integrated, end-to-end logistics network that enables rapid fulfillment and delivery of a vast selection of consumer goods.
linked_companies.evidence: Coupang operates primarily as a pure-play e-commerce enterprise, structured around its core Product Commerce segment, which most recently delivered $7.2 billion of the company's $8.5 billion consolidated net revenues. The company directs billions of dollars in capital expenditures into a proprietary logistics network, equipping dedicated teams to manage online retail operations and fulfillment infrastructure. To capture further market share and serve nearly 24 million active customers, Coupang scales its e-commerce ecosystem by integrating a first-party retail catalog with a faster-growing third-party marketplace powered by Fulfillment and Logistics by Coupang (FLC).
linked_companies.name: COUPANG INC

linked_companies.description: Operates a global online marketplace connecting buyers and sellers, facilitating digital retail through consumer-to-consumer and business-to-consumer transactions across both auction-style and fixed-price formats.
linked_companies.evidence: eBay operates as a pure-play global digital marketplace, with its core e-commerce infrastructure driving $3.09 billion in quarterly revenue and over $22.2 billion in gross merchandise volume. The company's organizational framework, led directly by its C-suite executives, is strictly designed to facilitate digital transactions for 136 million active buyers across more than 2.5 billion active listings. To scale this ecosystem and consistently outpace industry benchmarks, eBay dedicates 4% to 5% of its corporate revenue to capital expenditures while actively executing strategic platform acquisitions, such as the $1.2 billion purchase of Depop, to expand its consumer-to-consumer capabilities.
linked_companies.name: EBAY INC

linked_companies.description: Operates a global online retail marketplace that connects consumers with a vast selection of proprietary and third-party merchandise, supported by an extensive fulfillment and logistics infrastructure.
linked_companies.evidence: Amazon's organizational identity is fundamentally defined by its e-commerce business, which generated $143.9 billion across its North America and International segments in the second quarter of 2026, capturing nearly 80% of total revenue. This retail engine is driven by a 15% year-over-year increase in store units and a vast third-party marketplace, which recently expanded through global fee reductions and the deployment of AI-generated custom data visualizations in Seller Central. To sustain its operational scale and support millions of merchants, the company continuously directs multi-billion-dollar investments into supply chain improvements, large-format fulfillment centers, and artificial intelligence shopping tools like Rufus. These capacity enhancements, combined with ultra-fast delivery options and massive shopping events like Prime Day and the Big Spring Sale, establish a deeply integrated retail network that seamlessly connects consumers and third-party sellers.
linked_companies.name: AMAZON.COM INC

linked_companies.description: Operates a specialized digital retail platform for pet products and pharmacy services, advancing the e-commerce sector through direct-to-consumer fulfillment and automated subscription deliveries.
linked_companies.evidence: Chewy operates exclusively as a pure-play e-commerce platform, generating its entire $3.36 billion in recent quarterly net sales through retail websites and mobile applications. Positioning itself as the largest pet e-tailer in the United States, the company serves 21.5 million active customers and drives revenue consistency through its digital Autoship subscription program, which accounts for 84.4% of total sales. The company's organizational framework is entirely dedicated to supporting this online marketplace, utilizing large-scale fulfillment centers, digital bidding algorithms, and dedicated technologists to manage a highly scalable tech stack. Additionally, strategic financial allocations, such as $129.2 million in annual capital expenditures and the $175 million acquisition of SmartPak, are fundamentally designed to expand its e-commerce infrastructure and capitalize on secular shifts toward online consumer purchasing.
linked_companies.name: CHEWY INC - CLASS A

linked_companies.description: Operates a dedicated e-commerce platform focused on furniture and home goods, providing consumers with digital retail access to a vast selection of products from numerous global suppliers.
linked_companies.evidence: Wayfair operates as a pure-play digital marketplace, utilizing its primary platform, Wayfair.com, to connect home goods suppliers directly with retail consumers. This e-commerce infrastructure relies on a centralized technology organization of over 2,000 engineers and data scientists managing an online catalog of 40 million products. To maintain this digital-first retail delivery mechanism, the company routinely allocates capital expenditures, including $54 million in a recent quarter, toward global tech replatforming and native mobile applications. By functioning as an inventory-light platform that leverages supplier competition to optimize retail prices, Wayfair captures nearly the entirety of its revenue through digital transactions.
linked_companies.name: WAYFAIR INC- CLASS A

themes.description: Comprehensive marketing and distribution approach in retail involving multiple channels such as physical stores, online platforms, and mobile applications, ensuring a seamless consumer experience.

linked_companies.description: Integrates an extensive physical store network with digital e-commerce platforms to enable seamless customer experiences through services such as curbside pickup, same-day delivery, and unified inventory management.
linked_companies.evidence: Walmart positions its comprehensive omnichannel business model as the fundamental framework of its go-to-market strategy, explicitly designing it to serve customers however they choose to shop. To scale this integration of physical stores and digital platforms, the company deployed a $1.7 billion increase in capital expenditures in Q2 2026, building on a $2.9 billion omnichannel investment from the previous quarter. This sustained multi-billion dollar commitment directly translates into operational results, with store-fulfilled delivery driving a 5.2% comparable sales contribution to the Walmart U.S. segment and fueling a 26% increase in global e-commerce growth. The structural reliance on these proprietary pickup and delivery networks continually reinforces customer and Walmart+ member engagement across the retail ecosystem.
linked_companies.name: WALMART INC

linked_companies.description: Integrates a nationwide physical store network with digital platforms using a store-as-hub model, enabling seamless fulfillment options such as curbside pickup, in-store pickup, and same-day delivery to enhance the overall shopping experience.
linked_companies.evidence: Target operates under a unified retail strategy that seamlessly integrates its physical stores and digital channels to drive its entire merchandise revenue model. Utilizing a 'stores as hubs' approach across its nearly 2,000 locations, the company relies on its physical footprint to fulfill 97.6% of all merchandise sales. This highly integrated supply web efficiently manages digitally originated orders through services like Order Pickup, Drive Up, and Same Day Delivery, which account for two-thirds of all digital fulfillments. To support this single-segment business model, Target actively directs its capital expenditures toward supply chain and physical network enhancements, reinforcing an operation that yields substantial logistical and scale advantages.
linked_companies.name: TARGET CORP

linked_companies.description: Delivers unified commerce and supply chain software solutions that synchronize order management, inventory visibility, and store fulfillment to enable seamless customer experiences across physical and digital retail channels.
linked_companies.evidence: Manhattan Associates drives its omnichannel operations through its core Active Omni product suite, which recently secured the company's largest-ever Order Management System bookings deal. This proprietary platform aligns complex cross-channel fulfillment execution and catalyzed recent booking velocity by capturing new logo implementations with one of the world's largest retailers and a large auto parts distributor. To support this demand, the company directs a portion of its global workforce and a $37.3 million quarterly R&D investment toward enhancing its unified commerce architecture, introducing advanced simulation features that balance dynamic delivery speeds and distressed inventory markdowns. Sustained by these core capability developments across e-commerce and retail store operations, industry analysts including ARC Advisory Group and Gartner categorize Manhattan as a market leader in omnichannel software.
linked_companies.name: MANHATTAN ASSOCIATES INC

linked_companies.description: Operates a highly integrated direct-to-consumer model that bridges its digital e-commerce platform and virtual try-on technology with a growing footprint of physical retail stores to deliver a seamless shopping experience.
linked_companies.evidence: Warby Parker's integration of an omnichannel strategy is driven by management's explicit designation of scaling this model as the company's foremost strategic priority for 2026. The retailer processes 100% of its revenue through an interconnected ecosystem of e-commerce platforms and a growing physical footprint, recently adding 14 net new stores in a single quarter to surpass 330 total locations. To deepen this physical-digital alignment, the company directs capital toward cross-channel shopping infrastructure, pairing store build-outs and enhanced product displays with proprietary digital tools like Virtual Try-On and AI-powered recommendations. Ultimately, this framework seamlessly links physical product trials and in-store services with digital conversion pathways to dictate the company's core distribution capabilities.
linked_companies.name: WARBY PARKER INC-CLASS A

linked_companies.description: Integrates physical retail locations with e-commerce platforms, mobile applications, and a comprehensive loyalty program to deliver a seamless, unified beauty shopping experience across all customer touchpoints.
linked_companies.evidence: Ulta Beauty operates entirely within a single reportable segment that integrates its physical retail stores, salon services, and e-commerce platforms into a unified consumer ecosystem. The company relies on its "convenient omnichannel footprint" to drive revenue, continuously expanding "buy anywhere, fill anywhere" fulfillment capabilities such as Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPIS) and same-day delivery via Uber Eats. To support this infrastructure, capital expenditures are directly allocated to information technology and supply chain optimization, complementing digital extensions like mobile app sales and social commerce integrations through TikTok Shop. Management identifies this seamless blending of physical and digital operations as a core mechanism for achieving long-term growth and sustaining market share leadership.
linked_companies.name: ULTA BEAUTY INC

The company dedicates its entire workforce of over 1,200 employees to this flagship offering, actively advancing the platform through targeted artificial intelligence capabilities and an expanding offshore R&D facility in India. Alkami reinforces its technological presence by maintaining over 450 proprietary back-office integrations and recently deploying $375.5 million to acquire MANTL, deeply embedding advanced account opening and loan origination solutions directly into its financial institution ecosystem.

linked_companies.evidence: Q2 Holdings operates as a pure-play banking technology provider, delivering mission-critical digital platforms, fraud management solutions, and AI tools that allow financial institutions to modernize away from legacy systems. The company's unified, cloud-based software sits in the flow of all digital interactions, providing pre-built integrations that decouple front-end experiences from back-end core processors for over 500 customer accounts. This strategic positioning creates an entrenched structural moat, highlighted by an annual recurring revenue of $945 million and a 93% retention rate as the go-forward solution during post-merger core conversions. To sustain this foundational infrastructure, Q2 dedicates its workforce of over 2,500 employees toward continuous research and development, supported by specialized go-to-market and relationship management teams.

linked_companies.evidence: FIS operates as a foundational infrastructure provider for the financial services industry, delivering digital interfaces, AI architectures, and proprietary core software such as the Horizon system.
